title: Control plane DB surgery: schema normalization, safe migrations, and index tuning
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
We have accumulated schema cruft and unoptimized queries in the control plane primary DB (Postgres 13). This ticket covers a focused, low-risk program of work: normalize two hot tables (deployments, route_logs), add targeted indexes and partial indexes, replace a dozen slow view queries with materialized views where appropriate, and implement a safe online migration pattern to avoid long locks and downtime.

Goals:
- Reduce 95th percentile read latency on control plane read API paths by >=30% for high-traffic projects.
- Reduce daily CPU on primary DB by >=20% under typical load.
- Migrate schema without >2s p99 API regressions or longer than 5-minute maintenance windows.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Schema cleanup plan and migration scripts: split deploy_meta JSON blob into typed columns for fields used in queries; normalize route_logs by extracting event_type and adding timestamp sharding column.
2) Indexing: add partial indexes for active deployments and composite indexes for frequent join patterns; evaluate multi-column vs expression indexes.
3) Query changes: replace three frequently-run slow queries (dashboard counts, global quota check, recent-errors feed) with optimized SQL and one materialized view refreshed incrementally.
4) Telemetry: add DB-level metrics (pg_stat_statements top N, index usage, lock waits) to Console graphs and alert rules.
5) Migration orchestration: implement zero-downtime approach using dual-write, backfill workers, and short-lived constraint application with verification.
6) Rollout: canary by account tier (beta -> production), automated verification scripts and rollback plan.

High-level plan / tasks:
- (A) Investigate & profile current queries (Sergio) — Complete. Found top 12 queries accounting for 62% of CPU during spikes. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP-DB/top-queries
- (B) Design normalized schema and index candidates (Arjun/Sofia) — Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infer/controlplane/db-schema-surgery
- (C) Implement migration scripts with pg_repack-friendly operations and dual-write support (ENG: Arjun) — WIP. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1875
- (D) Create backfill workers and throttling knobs (ENG: Priya) — planned
- (E) Add telemetry panels and alerting (ENG: Sergio) — planned
- (F) Run staging rehearsal and measure perf delta; if >30% improvement on p95 proceed to canary (ENG + SRE) — planned

Acceptance criteria:
- Migration tested in staging without p99 regressions for API endpoints in the smoke suite (metrics captured).
- Backfill completes for 99% of rows within expected time window for a representative customer dataset (we used customer-sim dataset).
- Production canary shows >=20% CPU reduction and >=25% p95 latency reduction for control-plane read APIs.
- All schema changes covered by migration-safety checklist and signed off by SRE and Data Security.

Risk & mitigation:
- Long table locks during ALTER: mitigation is dual-write + backfill + swap via computed column + short transactional check. We will avoid a single ALTER TYPE on large tables.
- Index bloat and write amplification: use partial indexes and monitor write latency during canary, rollback if write-p50 increases >30%.
- Backfill causing replication lag: backfill worker has rate limit and monitors replica lag to pause.

Testing & verification:
- Unit tests for migration helpers; integration tests run migrations against a 10M-row synthetic dataset in CI.
- Performance smoke harness that executes 500 concurrent read-heavy requests and records p50/p95/p99. Harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane-bench
- Post-deploy verification script that checks row counts, index usage, and sample queries.

Rollback plan:
- If canary fails, toggle a feature-flag to route requests to pre-change read-replica; halt backfill; revert dual-write in 1 transaction; re-add previous indexes if needed. PRs will include a revert plan.

Notes / trade-offs:
- We intentionally avoid a full normalization of historical auditing tables due to cost; target only the hot path fields referenced in live queries.
- We chose partial indexes over global indexes to reduce write amplification.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finish PR #1875 with online migration harness (Arjun) — target code complete by 2026-03-15.
- Kick off backfill worker implementation (Priya) — 2d spike.
- SRE to schedule a staging rehearsal and enable pg_stat_statements on staging (Sergio).
